course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Globalization
unit.description: Study how technology, disease, and environmental change reshaped the world, how the global economy and culture developed, and how people and institutions responded to globalization.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of non-Western culture gaining a global audience?
choices: The spread of McDonald's restaurants to Asia
The popularity of Bollywood films in Africa
Hollywood films shown in European theaters
Coca-Cola sold in markets across Asia
questions.explanation: Indian films reached audiences across Asia and Africa.
choiceExplanations: Indian films reached audiences across Asia and Africa.
questions.distinguisher: McDonald's spread globally, but it is an American brand.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains the rapid global spread of Korean pop music?
choices: Trade along the old Silk Roads
questions.explanation: Online platforms let fans worldwide share and watch music.
choiceExplanations: Online platforms let fans worldwide share and watch music.
Korea was colonized, not a colonizer, in the twentieth century.
questions.distinguisher: Korea was ruled by Japan from 1910 to 1945, not a colonial power.

questions.prompt: Which claim about global culture after 1945 is most defensible?
questions.explanation: Indian, Jamaican, Japanese, and Korean culture spread too.
choiceExplanations: Indian, Jamaican, Japanese, and Korean culture spread too.
questions.distinguisher: American brands spread widely, but culture also flowed from elsewhere.

questions.prompt: The popularity of cricket in India and the Caribbean shows
choices: a continuity from the era of British imperialism
the lasting influence of the Mongol Empire
a rejection of British culture after independence
the spread of American culture after 1945
questions.explanation: Cricket spread through the British Empire and remained popular.
choiceExplanations: Cricket spread through the British Empire and remained popular.
questions.distinguisher: Former colonies kept cricket after independence and made it their own.

questions.prompt: Television and satellite broadcasting affected sports by
questions.distinguisher: Broadcasting expanded audiences rather than limiting them.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, critics of American brands worried about
choices: the decline of Hollywood's film studios
the end of social media platforms
choiceExplanations: Bollywood is presented as a counterexample.
The passage does not say that.
questions.distinguisher: Bollywood's success shows influence flowing toward the United States and others, not the critics' worry.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 9.6 key concept: popular and consumer culture became more global
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the spread of global consumer culture after 1950
stimulusBlocks.text:
After World War II, American brands such as Coca-Cola and McDonald's opened in country after country, and Hollywood films reached audiences worldwide. Critics warned of “Americanization,” the replacement of local cultures with American products.

Cultural influence also flowed in many directions. India's film industry, centered in Mumbai and known as Bollywood, produces more films each year than Hollywood and has audiences across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Japanese anime and South Korean pop music developed global fan bases, often spread by social media.

questions.prompt: The second paragraph of the passage is used to
choices: support the critics' argument about Americanization
qualify the claim that global culture was American
argue that Hollywood made more films than Bollywood
show that culture stopped spreading after 1950
questions.explanation: It shows culture flowing from India, Japan, and Korea.
choiceExplanations: It shows culture flowing from India, Japan, and Korea.
questions.distinguisher: The paragraph complicates the critics' view rather than supporting it.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, Bob Marley's reggae found audiences in Africa and Europe partly because of
choices: its songs about poverty and resistance
its use at the opening of the World Cup
its origins in Mumbai's film industry
questions.explanation: Its themes resonated with listeners far from Jamaica.
choiceExplanations: Its themes resonated with listeners far from Jamaica.
The passage does not link reggae to the World Cup.
The passage does not mention government support.
questions.distinguisher: Mumbai is the center of Bollywood; reggae came from Jamaica.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 9.6 key concept: arts, entertainment, and sports increasingly reflected the influence of a globalized society
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing global sports and music after 1960
stimulusBlocks.text:
Reggae music, which developed in Jamaica in the 1960s, spread worldwide through artists such as Bob Marley, whose songs about poverty and resistance found audiences in Africa and Europe.

Sports also became global. Hundreds of millions of people watch the FIFA World Cup, and cricket, spread by the British Empire, became a national passion in India, Pakistan, and the Caribbean. Players now move between leagues on different continents.

questions.prompt: The passage's description of cricket best illustrates
questions.explanation: Cricket spread through the British Empire and endured.
choiceExplanations: Cricket spread through the British Empire and endured.
questions.distinguisher: Former colonies kept cricket rather than rejecting it.
